receita-de-inferencia.d: A documented, reproducible set of decisions for serving a model on a given piece of hardware: engine image, checkpoint and weight format, patches/overlays, topology (TP/EP), engine arguments, speculation, and the verification and benchmark protocol — each with its reason and with measured numbers.

dgx-spark.d: NVIDIA's compact computer with the GB10 SoC (Blackwell sm_121 GPU + ARM CPU), a nominal 128 GB of LPDDR5X unified memory (a physical pool of 128 GiB, of which ~121.7 GiB are visible to CUDA; ~273 GB/s theoretical) and 200 Gb/s ConnectX-7 networking. The three recipes use two of them.

parametros-totais.d: All of the model's weights, including the experts a token doesn't use. They decide the memory needed (\( N_{\text{total}} \times b/8 \) bytes); decode speed depends on the active parameters.

conta-de-guardanapo.d: An order-of-magnitude estimate made before any launch: memory ≈ total parameters × the checkpoint's average bits ÷ 8, and decode ceiling ≈ bandwidth ÷ bytes read per step (active parameters × effective bits of what is read ÷ 8). It tells you whether it's worth trying; the measurement tells you the rest.

atencao-global.d: An attention layer in which each token can query all the previous ones; the KV grows linearly with the context. It contrasts with the sliding window (only the last W tokens), with sparse attention (only the tokens chosen by an indexer) and with linear attention (a fixed-size state).

mimo-v2-6-flash.d: Xiaomi's open MoE (Sep 2026; 309 B total / 15 B active): 48 hybrid layers with a window:global ratio of 39:9, K and V with different dimensions (192/128), native MXFP4 experts, a 3-layer MTP and a 5-layer DFlash drafter, 1M context. It is the model of the final tutorial (MOPD variant).

copilot.d: The platform's floating tutor (<kbd>⌘/Ctrl J</kbd>): it reads the visible section or chapter and talks to any server that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions contract — local MLX, your own vLLM recipe, OpenAI, OpenRouter, LM Studio or Ollama.

mlx.d: Apple's array framework (ml-explore) for Apple Silicon, which takes advantage of the Mac's unified memory. The mlx-lm package runs, quantizes and serves LLMs (the “4bit”, “8bit” and “MXFP4” suffixes in model names are quantization formats).

mlx-lm-server.d: The mlx-lm package's server, which exposes /v1/chat/completions and /v1/models (default port 8080, bound to 127.0.0.1, CORS open). It requires Python ≥ 3.10; if it receives a model id different from the loaded one, it switches models (and downloads it, if needed).

cors.d: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: the browser rule that only lets a page read responses from another origin if the server allows it (Access-Control-Allow-Origin). That's why Ollama and LM Studio need configuring for the copilot, and why serving the platform over http://localhost avoids the null origin of file://.
